one_liner: SSE4/AVX2 fork of Python's Pillow; resizes 8-bit RGB images 11-23x faster than ImageMagick 6 via Wand, single core.
what_it_does: A fork of Pillow that tracks upstream releases (version X.Y.Z.postN replaces Pillow X.Y.Z) and swaps hand-written SSE4/AVX2 kernels into libImaging for resize, box/Gaussian blur, 3x3 and 5x5 kernel filters, alpha compositing, premultiply/unpremultiply, RGB to L, split/getchannel, and (since the September 2026 re-port) ColorLUT and reduce. The Python API is unchanged: uninstall Pillow, install pillow-simd, and existing PIL code runs faster. It is not a C or C++ library; the kernels are only reachable through the CPython extension.
how_it_is_fast: Resampling is Pillow's separable two-pass convolution, but coefficients are quantised to INT16 with an adaptive precision (at most 15 bits) so each tap pair can go through _mm_madd_epi16/_mm256_madd_epi16 after a pshufb that interleaves RGBA bytes into 16-bit lanes. The horizontal pass processes four output rows at once (ImagingResampleHorizontalConvolution8u4x) with 4-tap unrolling, and the vertical pass works on 8 (AVX2) or 4 (SSE4) pixels per iteration. Other kernels use the same fixed-point integer SIMD pattern.
when_to_use: Python services that already use Pillow for thumbnails or resizing of 8-bit RGB/RGBA images on x86 and can build from source.
Downscaling large photos with bilinear, bicubic or Lanczos filters: the pillow-perf c5.large file shows 4.5-7.8x over Pillow 7.0.0 for downscales with the AVX2 build.
Pipelines that also lean on Pillow's filter(), box/Gaussian blur, alpha_composite or mode conversion, which have SIMD paths too.
Fleets where you control the CPU (AVX2 everywhere) and can compile per target, as Uploadcare does in production since 2015.
when_not_to_use: Anything outside Python, including C++ code: the SIMD kernels are not exposed as a standalone library.
ARM (Apple Silicon, Graviton) or other non-x86 hosts: setup.py adds -msse4 unconditionally and the build fails there (issues #116, #143); a RISC-V Vector PR (#158) is still open.
Grayscale (mode L), 16-bit (I;16) or float (I, F) images: in Resample.c only the 4-byte-per-pixel UINT8 path is vectorised; image8 and 16bpc paths stay scalar.

End-to-end pipelines dominated by decode and encode: in the same c5.large file, load+resize+save is only about 4.5x faster than Wand (0.039 s vs 0.176 s), and in the libvips wiki pipeline libvips is 2.6x faster than pillow-simd (0.57 s vs 1.51 s) because it threads and streams.
Binary-wheel deployments: PyPI carries only sdists, so every install needs a compiler and Pillow's native dependencies (zlib, libjpeg); issues #157 and #120 are zlib-not-found build failures.

integration.dependencies: CPython (or PyPy) >=3.10 for the 12.x line; build needs setuptools>=77, pybind11, a C compiler, and Pillow's native libraries (zlib and libjpeg required; libtiff, libwebp, freetype, lcms2 optional)
integration.min_toolchain: C compiler accepting -msse4 (GCC or Clang); AVX2 build via CC="cc -mavx2"; MSVC x64 gets the SSE4 path through a macro in ImagingSIMD.h
integration.platforms: x86 and x86-64 only (SSE4.1 required; AVX2 optional at build time, no runtime dispatch)
integration.thread_safety: Same as Pillow: resample kernels run inside ImagingSectionEnter/Leave, Pillow's GIL-release section, so different images can be processed on parallel threads; each operation itself is single-threaded
integration.drop_in_for_baseline: partial — drop-in for Pillow of the same version (pip uninstall pillow first), not for ImageMagick, whose API and filters differ

gotchas: The instruction set is fixed at compile time: an AVX2 build (CC="cc -mavx2") on a build host will crash with an illegal instruction on a CPU without AVX2, and the default build needs SSE4.1. There is no CPU check at import.

Output is not bit-identical to upstream Pillow: Pillow-SIMD normalises filter coefficients to INT16 with at most 15 bits of precision, while upstream Pillow uses INT32 coefficients with 22 bits (PRECISION_BITS), so some pixels can differ by rounding.
Installing it next to Pillow is unsupported; both provide the PIL package, so a later dependency that pulls in Pillow will silently overwrite the SIMD build.

Older pillow-simd releases lag upstream security fixes: PR #149 (ImageMath.eval environment restriction) has been open since 2024-10-08, and the libvips benchmark used 9.5.0; prefer a .post release of a current Pillow (12.1.1.post0 is on PyPI, the repo is at 12.3.0.post0).
pick_this_over_siblings_when: Pick it over libvips or OpenCV when the code base is already PIL-based Python and you want a speedup without rewriting calls; pick libvips for whole pipelines (2.6x faster than pillow-simd and far less memory in the libvips table), fast_image_resize for Rust, and OpenCV when bilinear upscaling dominates (cv2 single-threaded 0.052 s vs Pillow-SIMD AVX2 0.076 s to 5478x3424 in the same c5.large file).
verified_claims_summary: On an AWS c5.large, one core, a 2560x1600 RGB image resized with Pillow-SIMD 7.0.0.post3 built with -mavx2 took 0.00523 s to 320x200 (Lanczos) versus 0.10633 s for ImageMagick 6.9 through Wand with MAGICK_THREAD_LIMIT=1 (about 20x), and 11-23x across all 12 size and filter cases; compiler, exact CPU and Python overhead in the Wand path are not controlled, and ImageMagick works in 16-bit quantum. The independent libvips crop, 10% bilinear shrink, sharpen and save pipeline on a Threadripper PRO 3955WX timed pillow-simd 9.5.0 (installed with plain pip, so the default SSE4 build) at 1.51 s against ImageMagick 7.1.1 convert at 4.44 s (about 2.9x).
status_note: Active: SIMD kernels were re-landed on Pillow 12.3.0 on 2026-09-17 and sdists up to 12.1.1.post0 were uploaded to PyPI on 2026-09-15 after a two-year gap at 9.5.0, but there are still no wheels; MIT-CMU licensed and maintained mainly by one Uploadcare developer (homm).
